title: Trump Brokers 3-Day Russia-Ukraine Ceasefire (May 9–11) with 1,000-for-1,000 POW Exchange
detail: President Trump announced on May 9 that both Zelensky and Putin had agreed to a US-brokered 3-day ceasefire running May 9–11, timed to coincide with Russia's Victory Day celebrations. The agreement includes a 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner-of-war exchange — the largest in the war. Trump called it 'the beginning of the end' of the war. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov confirmed Russia's acceptance; Zelensky confirmed through the Ukrainian president's office. The ceasefire covers a full halt to kinetic operations — ground assaults, drone strikes, and missile fire — for all three days. This ceasefire is separate from earlier unilateral ceasefires declared by both sides in the May 4–8 window, which collapsed within hours. Despite the announcement, both sides continued to accuse each other of violations within hours of the truce taking effect: Russia claimed Ukraine committed 8,970 violations (including drone and artillery fire); Ukraine documented continued Russian drone and missile launches.

media.caption: Trump announces US-brokered 3-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, May 9–11, 2026

title: Russia Launches Iskander-M Ballistic Missile + 43 Strike Drones at Ukraine on Day 1 of Ceasefire
detail: Despite the Trump-brokered ceasefire taking effect on May 9, Russia launched continued strikes against Ukraine. Russia's overnight attack included 1 Iskander-M ballistic missile and 43 Shahed-type strike drones targeting six Ukrainian locations. A father and son were killed in a drone strike on an agricultural enterprise in Chernihiv region — making civilian deaths on the very first day of the proclaimed truce. Russia's Defense Ministry counter-claimed Ukraine had committed 8,970 ceasefire violations since midnight, including 1,173 artillery/MLRS/mortar/tank attacks and 7,151 drone strikes — figures treated with skepticism by Western analysts given their extraordinary scale. Ukraine's Foreign Ministry documented 108 Russian combat drone and 3 missile strikes during the prior ceasefire window (May 5–6), establishing a pattern of Russian non-compliance with declared ceasefires throughout the May period.

media.caption: Russia fires Iskander-M ballistic missile and 43 drones at Ukraine on first day of Trump-brokered ceasefire, killing civilians in Chernihiv — May 9, 2026

title: Ukrainian Drones Strike Yaroslavl Oil Refinery and Rostov-on-Don on Night of Ceasefire Announcement
detail: On the night of May 9, as the Trump-brokered ceasefire was formally announced, Ukrainian drones struck an oil refinery in Yaroslavl (approximately 1,000 km from Ukraine) and triggered explosions near defense-linked sites in Rostov-on-Don. The Yaroslavl refinery strike caused a fire visible from several kilometers away. These strikes extended Ukraine's ongoing deep-strike campaign that included the Perm refinery (struck May 8, the third time in two weeks) and the Caspian Sea naval base in Kaspiysk (May 8). The near-simultaneous strikes on critical Russian energy and logistics infrastructure — paired with the ceasefire announcement — put both the timing and Ukraine's intent under intense scrutiny, with Ukrainian officials framing the attacks as retaliation for Russia's continued attacks during prior Ukrainian-declared ceasefires.

media.caption: Ukrainian drones strike Yaroslavl oil refinery and targets near Rostov-on-Don as ceasefire announced — May 9, 2026

title: Zelensky Issues Mock 'Decree' Excluding Red Square Coordinates from Ukraine's Strike Targets During Parade
detail: President Zelensky issued a pointed public 'decree' on May 9, formally and satirically 'permitting' Russia to hold its Victory Day parade and specifically excluding the exact military grid coordinates of Red Square in Moscow from Ukraine's targeting plan during parade hours (10:00 a.m. Kyiv time). The decree pointedly included the precise military coordinates of Red Square — widely interpreted as a diplomatic taunt demonstrating Ukraine's capacity to strike the Russian capital. Ukrainian social media and the presidential office framed this as a demonstration of Ukraine's restraint and its ability to choose when and where to strike inside Russia. The mock decree was covered broadly by Western media as an act of psychological warfare, underscoring Ukraine's deep-strike capability and contrasting it with Russia's continued attacks on Ukrainian civilian infrastructure throughout the 'ceasefire' period.

media.caption: Zelensky issues satirical 'decree' listing exact coordinates of Red Square — excluded from Ukrainian strikes during Victory Day parade — May 9, 2026
